ei.title: Opening Up the Web to Everyone
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Opening Up the Web to Everyone Imagine you have fallen down and broken your right arm. There are some things that would be difficult to do with your injured arm. For example, you might not be able to carry heavy boxes or ride your bike. What about accessing the Internet? If you are right-handed, using a computer mouse or touchscreen with your left hand would be awkward and take a lot of time. However, this is a minor challenge compared to what some of us face on the Internet. For people with certain disabilities, many websites can be nearly impossible to use. This is the reason why web accessibility is important. Web accessibility is the practice of making sure that websites can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities. So what exactly makes a website accessible? Here are some common features of accessible websites. Text Descriptions of Images Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images. Sometimes such visual information is important for understanding the text. This is a problem for users with visual disabilities. When they go on a website, they often use programs called “screen readers,” which read online text aloud. However, these programs cannot “read” images. Accessible websites solve this problem by providing alternative text, also known as “alt text.” Alt text is a brief description of non-textual information. For instance, if an image shows a group of students, its alt text would explain how many students are in the image and what they are doing. Screen readers can detect this alt text and read it aloud. This way, alt text ensures that people with visual disabilities can access more of the information on a website. Transcripts and Captions for Multimedia Content In some cases, audio content cannot be accessed or understood. Some people may have hearing disabilities, while others might be in places where they can’t listen to audio, such as a quiet library. Therefore, accessible websites often offer other ways to access information that is presented in audio form. For example, they may provide transcripts or captions that can help users access this information. Transcripts are text versions of the entire audio content, while captions are text versions of the audio that appear in a video as it plays. Captions include not only the text version of the spoken words but also descriptions of the music and other sounds in the video. Content That Is Easy to See and Hear Having a visual disability doesn’t necessarily mean a person can’t see at all. Some people, including many elderly people, simply have poor eyesight. This makes it difficult for them to read. For this reason, accessible websites have a background color that contrasts with the color of their text. This makes the text clear enough for most people to see. As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to adjust the volume of background sound or to turn it off altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites. Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that limit the movement of their hands. They rely on their keyboards, rather than a mouse, to navigate websites. On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard. This means that links, buttons, and fields, which are spaces where information is entered, can be accessed through keyboard navigation. Users navigate the websites by making use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key. For example, they can use the tab key to jump from one part of a web page to another. Both users with disabilities and those with temporarily injured hands can benefit from this kind of navigation. Indicators Other than Color That Convey Information Color blindness is a common visual disability. People with color blindness find it difficult to tell some colors apart. This can cause problems, especially when graphs and charts only use colors to show the differences between sets of information. Accessible websites use other indicators along with the colors. For example, a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is solid. This ensures that everyone can tell the two lines apart. The accessibility features of websites don’t just help people with disabilities. They can make online experiences easier for everyone, regardless of abilities or situations. When websites are easy to navigate and understand, we can all benefit from a more inclusive online experience.

questions.passage: Opening Up the Web to Everyone Imagine you have fallen down and broken your right arm. There are some things that would be difficult to do with your (A)[injured / healthy] arm. For example, you might not be able to carry heavy boxes or ride your bike. What about accessing the Internet? If you are right-handed, using a computer mouse or touchscreen with your left hand would be (B)[comfortable / awkward] and take a lot of time. However, this is a (C)[major / minor] challenge compared to what some of us face on the Internet. For people with certain disabilities, many websites can be nearly impossible to use. This is the reason why web accessibility is important.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① healthy(건강한)는 팔이 부러졌다는 문맥과 반대
✅ ② injured(다친)+awkward(어색한)+minor(사소한) ← 정답
❌ ③ comfortable(편안한)은 왼손으로 마우스를 쓰면 불편하다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ major(중대한)는 장애인이 겪는 어려움에 비하면 사소한 문제라는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: injured=다친, awkward=어색한/불편한, minor=사소한

questions.passage: Text Descriptions of Images Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images. Sometimes such visual information is important for (A)[understanding / ignoring] the text. This is a problem for users with visual disabilities. When they go on a website, they often use programs called “screen readers,” which read online text aloud. However, these programs cannot “read” images. Accessible websites (B)[cause / solve] this problem by providing alternative text, also known as “alt text. ” Alt text is a (C)[lengthy / brief] description of non-textual information. For instance, if an image shows a group of students, its alt text would explain how many students are in the image and what they are doing. Screen readers can detect this alt text and read it aloud. This way, alt text ensures that people with visual disabilities can access more of the information on a website.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① ignoring(무시하는 것)은 시각 정보가 글 이해에 중요하다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② cause(일으키다)는 접근성 좋은 웹사이트가 문제를 해결한다는 문맥과 반대, lengthy(장황한)도 부적절
❌ ③ ignoring과 cause 모두 문맥과 반대
✅ ④ understanding(이해하는 것)+solve(해결하다)+brief(간략한) ← 정답
det.tip: understanding=이해(하는 것), solve=해결하다, brief=간략한

questions.passage: Content That Is Easy to See and Hear Having a visual disability doesn’t necessarily mean a person can’t see at all. Some people, including many elderly people, simply have (A)[poor / perfect] eyesight. This makes it difficult for them to read. For this reason, accessible websites have a background color that (B)[blends / contrasts] with the color of their text. This makes the text clear enough for most people to see. As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to (C)[ignore / adjust] the volume of background sound or to turn it off altogether. This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① poor(나쁜)+contrasts(대비되다)+adjust(조절하다) ← 정답
❌ ② perfect(완벽한)는 글 읽기가 어렵다는 뒤 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ blends(섞이다)는 글자가 잘 보이게 배경색이 대비된다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다)는 사용자가 음량을 조절하게 해 준다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: poor eyesight=나쁜 시력, contrast with=~와 대비되다, adjust=조절하다

questions.passage: Opening Up the Web to Everyone Imagine you have fallen down and broken your right arm.  There are some things that would be ①<u>difficult</u> to do with your injured arm.  For example, you might not be able to carry ②<u>heavy</u> boxes or ride your bike.  What about accessing the Internet?  If you are right-handed, using a computer mouse or touchscreen with your left hand would be awkward and take a lot of time.  However, this is a minor challenge compared to what some of us face on the Internet.  For people with certain disabilities, many websites can be nearly impossible to use.  This is the reason why web accessibility is ③<u>useless</u>.  Web accessibility is the practice of making sure that websites can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities.  So what exactly makes a website ④<u>accessible</u>?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ useless → important: 웹 접근성이 중요하다(important)는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① difficult: 다친 팔로는 하기 어려운 일이 있다 적절
✅ ② heavy: 무거운 상자를 나르지 못할 수 있다 적절
❌ ③ useless(쓸모없는) → important(중요한) ← 정답: 장애가 있는 사람에게 많은 웹사이트가 거의 사용 불가능하므로 웹 접근성이 중요하다는 문맥
✅ ④ accessible: 무엇이 웹사이트를 접근 가능하게 만드는가 적절
det.tip: important(중요한) ↔ useless(쓸모없는)

questions.passage: Text Descriptions of Images Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images.  Sometimes such visual information is important for understanding the text.  This is a ①<u>problem</u> for users with visual disabilities.  When they go on a website, they often use programs called “screen readers,” which read online text ②<u>aloud</u>.  However, these programs cannot “read” images.  Accessible websites solve this problem by providing ③<u>alternative</u> text, also known as “alt text. ” Alt text is a brief description of non-textual information.  For instance, if an image shows a group of students, its alt text would explain how many students are in the image and what they are doing.  Screen readers can ④<u>ignore</u> this alt text and read it aloud.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ ignore → detect: 스크린 리더가 대체 텍스트를 감지해서(detect) 소리 내어 읽음
det.analysis:
✅ ① problem: 시각 장애가 있는 사용자에게는 문제 적절
✅ ② aloud: 온라인 텍스트를 소리 내어 읽는다 적절
✅ ③ alternative: 대체 텍스트(alt text)를 제공한다 적절
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다) → detect(감지하다) ← 정답: 스크린 리더가 alt text를 감지해서 소리 내어 읽어 주는 문맥이므로 무시한다는 부적절
det.tip: detect(감지하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)

questions.passage: Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that ①<u>limit</u> the movement of their hands.  They ②<u>rely</u> on their keyboards, rather than a mouse, to navigate websites.  On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard.  This means that links, buttons, and fields, which are spaces where information is ③<u>erased</u>, can be accessed through keyboard navigation.  Users navigate the websites by making use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key.  For example, they can use the tab key to jump from one part of a web page to another.  Both users with disabilities and those with temporarily injured hands can ④<u>benefit</u> from this kind of navigation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ erased → entered: fields는 정보가 입력되는(entered) 공간
det.analysis:
✅ ① limit: 손의 움직임을 제한하는 장애 적절
✅ ② rely: 마우스 대신 키보드에 의존한다 적절
❌ ③ erased(지워지는) → entered(입력되는) ← 정답: fields는 정보가 입력되는 공간이므로 지워진다는 부적절
✅ ④ benefit: 일시적으로 손을 다친 사용자도 혜택을 본다 적절
det.tip: entered(입력되는) ↔ erased(지워지는)

questions.passage: Opening Up the Web to Everyone Imagine you have fallen down and __________ your right arm.  There are some things that would be difficult to do with your injured arm.  For example, you might not be able to carry heavy boxes or ride your bike.  What about accessing the Internet?  If you are right-handed, using a computer mouse or touchscreen with your left hand would be awkward and take a lot of time.  However, this is a minor challenge compared to what some of us face on the Internet.  For people with certain disabilities, many websites can be nearly impossible to use.  This is the reason why web accessibility is important.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① broken: 넘어져서 오른팔이 부러진 상황 ← 정답: 뒤에 '다친(injured) 팔'이 이어짐
❌ ② folded: 접은 — 다쳤다는 뒤 문맥과 맞지 않아 부적합
❌ ③ raised: 들어 올린 — 다친 상황이 아니므로 부적합
❌ ④ decorated: 장식한 — 팔을 다친 문맥과 무관하여 부적합
det.tip: fallen down and broken your right arm: 넘어져서 오른팔이 부러짐 (injured arm과 연결)

questions.passage: Transcripts and Captions for Multimedia Content In some cases, audio content cannot be accessed or understood.  Some people may have __________ disabilities, while others might be in places where they can’t listen to audio, such as a quiet library.  Therefore, accessible websites often offer other ways to access information that is presented in audio form.  For example, they may provide transcripts or captions that can help users access this information.  Transcripts are text versions of the entire audio content, while captions are text versions of the audio that appear in a video as it plays.  Captions include not only the text version of the spoken words but also descriptions of the music and other sounds in the video.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① visual: 시각의 — 오디오 콘텐츠에 대한 문맥이므로 부적합
✅ ② hearing: 청각의 ← 정답: 오디오 콘텐츠를 들을 수 없는 경우를 설명하는 문맥
❌ ③ walking: 보행의 — 오디오 접근과 무관하여 부적합
❌ ④ learning: 학습의 — 듣기 문제와 무관하여 부적합
det.tip: hearing disabilities: 청각 장애 (audio content cannot be accessed와 연결)

questions.passage: Indicators Other than Color That Convey Information Color blindness is a common visual disability.  People with color blindness find it difficult to tell some colors apart.  This can cause problems, especially when graphs and charts only use colors to show the differences between sets of information.  Accessible websites use other indicators along with the colors.  For example, a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is __________.  This ensures that everyone can tell the two lines apart.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① dotted: 점선의 — 초록 선이 이미 점선이므로 구별이 안 되어 부적합
❌ ② curved: 구부러진 — 선 모양으로 두 선을 구별하는 문맥이지만 원문 단서와 맞지 않음
✅ ③ solid: 실선의 ← 정답: 초록 선은 점선, 파란 선은 실선으로 구별
❌ ④ colorful: 알록달록한 — 색 이외의 표시로 구별한다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is solid: 점선 ↔ 실선 대비

questions.passage: Some people may have hearing disabilities, while others might be in places where they can’t listen to audio, such as a quiet library.  Therefore, accessible websites often offer other ways to access information that is presented in audio form.  For example, they may provide transcripts or captions that can help users access this information.  Transcripts are text versions of the <u>entire</u> audio content, while captions are text versions of the audio that appear in a video as it plays.  Captions include not only the text version of the spoken words but also descriptions of the music and other sounds in the video.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 entire와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① whole: 전체의 ← 정답: 오디오 콘텐츠 전체의 텍스트 버전
❌ ② partial: 부분적인 — 전체와 반대이므로 부적합
❌ ③ recorded: 녹음된 — 전체라는 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
❌ ④ spoken: 말로 된 — 전체라는 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
det.tip: the entire audio content = the whole audio content = 오디오 콘텐츠 전체

questions.passage: Accessible websites solve this problem by providing alternative text, also known as “alt text. ” Alt text is a brief description of non-textual information.  For instance, if an image shows a group of students, its alt text would explain how many students are in the image and what they are doing.  Screen readers can detect this alt text and read it aloud.  This way, alt text <u>ensures</u> that people with visual disabilities can access more of the information on a website.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ensures와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① prevents: 막다 — 보장과 반대 방향이므로 부적합
❌ ② doubts: 의심하다 — 확실하게 한다는 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
❌ ③ delays: 지연시키다 — 보장의 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
✅ ④ guarantees: 보장하다 ← 정답: alt text가 시각 장애인이 정보에 접근할 수 있도록 보장함
det.tip: ensure = guarantee = 반드시 ~하게 하다, 보장하다

questions.passage: This makes it difficult for them to read.  For this reason, accessible websites have a background color that contrasts with the color of their text.  This makes the text clear enough for most people to see.  As for audio content, accessible websites allow users to adjust the volume of background sound or to turn it off <u>altogether</u>.  This gives users both with and without hearing difficulties more control over their experience while they are using the sites.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 altogether와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① suddenly: 갑자기 — 정도가 아니라 시간을 나타내므로 부적합
✅ ② completely: 완전히 ← 정답: 배경 소리를 완전히 꺼 버리다
❌ ③ quietly: 조용히 — 완전히 끈다는 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
❌ ④ partially: 부분적으로 — 완전히와 반대이므로 부적합
det.tip: turn it off altogether = turn it off completely = 완전히 꺼 버리다

questions.passage: Web accessibility is the practice of making sure that websites can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities.  So what exactly makes a website accessible?  Here are some <u>common</u> features of accessible websites.  Text Descriptions of Images Along with text, most websites include other forms of information, such as images.  Sometimes such visual information is important for understanding the text.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 common와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① frequent: 빈번한 (common과 비슷한 뜻인 함정)
❌ ② simple: 단순한 (의미축 다름)
✅ ③ rare: 드문 ← 정답: 흔한(common)과 반대
❌ ④ modern: 현대적인 (의미축 다름)
det.tip: common(흔한) ↔ rare(드문)

questions.passage: On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard.  This means that links, buttons, and fields, which are spaces where information is entered, can be accessed through keyboard navigation.  Users navigate the websites by making use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key.  For example, they can use the tab key to jump from one part of a web page to another.  Both users with disabilities and those with <u>temporarily</u> injured hands can benefit from this kind of navigation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 temporarily와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① briefly: 잠깐 (temporarily와 비슷한 뜻인 함정)
✅ ② permanently: 영구적으로 ← 정답: 일시적으로(temporarily)와 반대
❌ ③ recently: 최근에 (시간 축이지만 반대 개념 아님)
❌ ④ carefully: 조심스럽게 (의미축 다름)
det.tip: temporarily(일시적으로) ↔ permanently(영구적으로)

questions.passage:
(A) Web accessibility is the <u>practice</u> of making sure that websites can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities. Many companies consider it a basic rule of good design.
(B) Using a keyboard quickly without looking takes a lot of <u>practice</u>. If you try it every day, your typing will get much faster.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 practice의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) the practice of making sure = 확실히 하는 관행/실천, (B) takes a lot of practice = 많은 연습이 필요하다 ← 정답
❌ ② (A)와 (B)의 의미가 서로 바뀜
❌ ③ (A)는 의사·변호사의 개업이 아니라 관행/실천
❌ ④ (B)는 개업이 아니라 매일 하는 연습
det.tip: practice: (A) 관행/실천 (the practice of V-ing) / (B) 연습 (takes practice)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to change something slightly in order to make it more suitable or effective"

det.analysis:
❌ ① maintain: 유지하다 — 바꾸는 것이 아니므로 부적합
❌ ② remove: 없애다 — 약간 바꾸는 것이 아니라 제거이므로 부적합
❌ ③ measure: 측정하다 — 바꾸는 뜻이 아니므로 부적합
✅ ④ adjust: 조절하다 — 더 알맞게 만들기 위해 약간 바꾸다 ← 정답 (adjust the volume)
det.tip: adjust = 알맞게 조금 바꾸다, 조절하다 (adjust the volume of background sound)

questions.passage: __________ (have) a visual disability doesn’t necessarily mean a person can’t see at all. Some people, including many elderly people, simply have poor eyesight. This makes it difficult for them to read.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 빈칸은 문장의 주어 자리이고 뒤에 동사 doesn’t necessarily mean이 이어진다. 동사 have가 주어 역할을 하려면 동명사 Having으로 바꿔야 한다. 'Having a visual disability(시각 장애가 있다는 것)' 전체가 주어: have → Having. (1단어) 조건이므로 to부정사는 불가
det.tip: 동명사(V-ing) 주어: Having a visual disability = 시각 장애가 있다는 것

questions.passage: Transcripts are text versions of the entire audio content, while captions are text versions of the audio that appear in a video as it plays. Captions include not only the text version of the spoken words but also __________ (describe) of the music and other sounds in the video.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 'not only A but also B' 병렬 구조에서 A가 명사구(the text version)이므로 B 자리에도 명사가 와야 한다. 또한 바로 뒤에 of the music이 이어지므로 '~에 대한 설명'이라는 명사가 필요하다. 동사 describe를 명사 descriptions로 변환: describe → descriptions
det.tip: not only A but also B 병렬: but also 뒤에도 명사형 (descriptions of ~ = ~에 대한 설명)

questions.passage: Complete Navigation Using the Keyboard Some users have disabilities that limit the movement of their hands.  They rely on their keyboards, __________ a mouse, to navigate websites.  On accessible websites, users can access everything on the site using only a keyboard.  This means that links, buttons, and fields, which are spaces where information is entered, can be accessed through keyboard navigation.  Users navigate the websites by making use of keys such as the space bar, the arrow keys, the enter key, and the tab key.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① in addition to: ~에 더하여 — 마우스도 함께 쓴다는 뜻이 되어 부적합
✅ ② rather than: ~ 대신에 ← 정답: 손 움직임이 제한된 사용자는 마우스 대신 키보드에 의존함
❌ ③ thanks to: ~ 덕분에 — 의존 대상의 대조가 아니므로 부적합
❌ ④ in spite of: ~에도 불구하고 — 대조·양보 모두 문맥에 맞지 않아 부적합
det.tip: rely on their keyboards, rather than a mouse: 마우스가 아니라 키보드에 의존 (대조)

questions.passage: For example, a line in green may also be dotted, while a line in blue is solid.  This ensures that everyone can tell the two lines apart.  The accessibility features of websites don’t just help people with disabilities.  They can make online experiences easier for everyone, __________ abilities or situations.  When websites are easy to navigate and understand, we can all benefit from a more inclusive online experience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① depending on: ~에 따라 — 모두에게 도움이 된다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② in terms of: ~의 측면에서 — '모두를 위한'이라는 포괄의 뜻이 없어 부적합
✅ ③ regardless of: ~에 상관없이 ← 정답: 능력이나 상황에 상관없이 모든 사람의 온라인 경험을 더 쉽게 만듦
❌ ④ in favor of: ~에 찬성하여 — 문맥과 무관하여 부적합
det.tip: for everyone, regardless of abilities or situations: 능력·상황에 상관없이 모두에게
